title: Imaging the early zebrafish embryo centrosomes following injection of small-molecule inhibitors to understand spindle formation
protocol: Dilute the solution to be injected before beginning.
Prepare 10 μL of solution so that there is extra in case of needle breakage.
Turn the injector on and open the gas tank.
Let the injection plate warm up to 20°C–23°C.
Load the injection solution into the needle using a pipette and needle-loading pipette tips.
Verify there is minimal air present at the end of the needle by ensuring the pipette tip reaches the end.
Remove any air bubbles in the injection solution using pipette suction if present.
Unscrew the barrel piece from micromanipulator.
Insert the flat end of the needle into the barrel piece.
Screw the barrel back onto the micromanipulator.
Pull dividers the morning after fish are set up for breeding.
Move the inner mesh-bottomed tank (with divider) to another outer tank with new system water.
Remove the divider to allow fish to mix and breed.
Collect embryos by placing the inner mesh-bottomed tank (containing fish) into a separate outer tank filled with system water.
Pour system water containing embryos through a white mesh net to collect them.
Fill empty tank with more system water and run it through the white mesh net again to ensure all embryos are collected.
Fill a Petri dish with embryo water.
Label the Petri dish with parent’s transgenic line and date of birth for the embryos.
Reverse the white mesh net to have the embryos facing outward toward the water.
Gently touch the embryos to the water within the Petri dish.
Bring embryos to injection station.
Add embryo water to the injection plate.
Transfer the embryos carefully to the plate using a transfer pipette.
Using a glass pipette with a melted tip, carefully push the embryos into the troughs.
Cut the needle with forceps using the Stereomicroscope.
Verify that the needle is no longer fused after cutting.
Cut the needle by forceps to determine its thickness/flexibility.
Check if the needle is too thin or causing significant damage to the embryo; adjust as necessary.
Zoom into 5× magnification on the microscope.
Adjust injection time and pressure until a liquid droplet of 6 μm in diameter is formed (approximately 1 nL).
Gently turn the balance knob to maintain a consistent droplet size.
Ensure troughs run at a diagonal to avoid puncturing the agarose and breaking the needle.
Position the needle so that only the x axis knob on the micromanipulator is needed for adjustment.
Puncture the embryo's yolk with the needle.
Press the foot pedal to inject.
Remove the needle from the embryo before adjusting the plate position.
Move the plate to the next embryo after each injection.
Adjust the micromanipulator to raise the needle as high as possible above the plate.
Remove the needle from the micromanipulator and dispose of it in the sharps container.
Use a glass pipette with a melted tip to remove embryos from their troughs.
Dislodge the embryo by pushing it upwards and collect it in a 60 mm petri-plate.
Incubate the collected embryos at 28.5°C until fixing or imaging is required.
Rinse the agarose plate with DI water after injection.
Store the rinsed agarose plate upside down in the refrigerator.
Turn off the microinjector and close the gas tank after completing injections.
Mount embryos for live imaging if a transgenic line or embryo with fluorescently tagged structures is available.
Wait until the embryos reach the 4-cell stage.
Move the embryos to a matTek plate containing a glass coverslip bottom using a disposable transfer pipette.
Remove as much embryo water as possible from the matTek plate.
Add approximately 300–500 μL of low melting point agarose to the matTek plate coverslip.
Ensure that the agarose has cooled slightly before covering the embryos but remains liquid enough not to harm them.
Spread the agarose using a 1 mL syringe needle to completely cover the glass coverslip and embryos.
Using the tip of the syringe needle, rotate the embryos so that the cells are facing downwards.
Ensure gentleness to avoid piercing the chorion with the syringe needle.
Gently push the embryos using the syringe needle to place them close to the coverslip.
Allow the agarose to solidify for 1-2 minutes.
Add embryo water to the matTek dish to prevent the agarose from over drying and shrinking while imaging.
Embryos are ready for immediate live imaging.
Move embryos to a matTek plate when they reach the 4-cell stage.
Remove as much embryo water as possible.
Add ∼300–500 μL low melting point agarose.
Spread the agarose with a 1 mL syringe needle to cover the embryos and coverslip of the matTek plate.
Rotate the embryos so that the cells face downwards toward the coverslip.
Gently push the embryos using the needle to place them close to the coverslip.
Allow the agarose to solidify.
Add embryo water to the matTek dish to prevent agarose from over drying and shrinking during imaging.
Transfer embryos into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube once at the desired developmental stage.
Replace embryo water with fixing solution pre-warmed to 28.5°C.
Incubate embryos in fixing solution for 2 hours at 20°C–23°C with frequent and gentle agitation.
Incubate tubes containing embryos and fixing solution at 4°C for 8–24 hours.
Remove fixing solution from embryos.
Wash embryos three times with PBST, each for 5 minutes.
Transfer embryos into a 60 mm plate containing PBST.
Dechorionate the embryos using forceps with thin tips.
Transfer dechorionated embryos back into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Remove PBST from the embryos.
Block embryos by adding 1 mL of fish wash solution.
Incubate embryos in fish wash solution for 1 hour at 20°C–23°C.
Remove fish wash solution and incubate embryos in 200 μL primary antibody solution (diluted to 1:200 in fish wash solution).
Optionally, incubate embryos with primary antibody solution for 4 hours at 20°C–23°C or for 8–24 hours at 4°C.
Wash embryos five times with fish wash solution, each for 5 minutes.
Incubate embryos in fish wash solution for 30–60 minutes at 20°C–23°C to block.
Remove fish wash solution and incubate embryos in secondary antibody diluted to 1:200 in wash solution.
Optionally, incubate embryos with secondary antibody for 8–24 hours at 4°C if primary antibodies were also incubated overnight or for 3–4 hours at 20°C–23°C.
Remove secondary antibody solution.
Wash embryos five times with fish wash solution, each for 5 minutes.
Incubate embryos in DAPI diluted 1:1,000 in 1× PBS for 1.5 hours at 20°C–23°C (optional).
Wash embryos three times with 1× PBS, each for 5 minutes.
Move fixed and stained embryos to a matTek plate containing a glass coverslip bottom using a disposable transfer pipette.
Remove as much embryo water as possible from the matTek plate using a 1 mL syringe with needle.
Add approximately 300–500 μL of low melting agarose to the matTek plate coverslip.
Spread the agarose to cover the embryos and coverslip of the matTek plate completely, ensuring contact at all edges.
Rotate the embryos so that the cells face down toward the coverslip using the tip of a syringe needle.
Gently push the embryos as close to the coverslip as possible using the syringe needle.
Allow the agarose to solidify for 1–2 minutes.
Add embryo water to prevent the agarose from over-drying and shrinking during imaging.
Embryos are ready for imaging.
Place embryos on glass slide.
Use two 1 mL syringes attached to 28-gauge × 0.5 inch needles to separate the cell mass from the yolk.
Hold one end of the cell mass with one needle while lifting the other end, separating cells and yolk.
Repeat separation for every embryo.
Remove excess yolk using a transfer pipette.
Ensure minimal yolk debris remains on the slide for clear imaging.
Flip the embryo so that the tops of the cells are facing away from the glass slide.
Remove as much PBS as possible using a 1 mL syringe.
Add 40 μL of ProLong to one side of the cells on the glass slide.
Place a No. 1.5 square (22 mm) coverslip on the same side, making sure it touches the ProLong.
Slowly lower the coverslip and apply gentle pressure to ensure cells are flattened and ProLong is distributed across the coverslip and embryos.
Avoid air bubbles.
Allow ProLong on slides to harden for 24 h at 20°C–23°C and in the dark before imaging.
